old_html_inputs: The Private Capital Colonization; The Spread Machine; The Cash Harvest
first_principles_point: A capital platform matters when it controls source capital, legal wrappers, origination, allocation, fees, spread, collateral, servicing, and claims on future cash.
money_path: saver/pension/insurer/institution/wealth client/retail investor/bank -> capital platform -> ETF/fund/insurer/BDC/SMA/private vehicle/credit facility/infrastructure fund/real-estate fund/ABS wrapper -> borrower/asset/project/security -> use of proceeds -> cash event -> waterfall -> platform and investor return
company_examples: BlackRock; Blackstone; KKR; Apollo/Athene; Ares; Brookfield; Carlyle; Blue Owl
proof_needed: AUM; FPAUM; inflows; insurance liabilities; vehicle schedule; borrower list; collateral; debt waterfall; realizations; spread; deployment; exits
safe_use: Use as a no-background capital-routing frame, not as proof that AUM or deployment equals named-cash realization.

first_principles_point: AUM proves routing scale, not named-cash realization.
money_path: capital source -> AUM category -> strategy or wrapper -> destination class -> named asset proof still missing
company_examples: BlackRock; Blackstone; KKR; Apollo; Brookfield; Ares; Carlyle
proof_needed: AUM; fee-paying AUM; strategy mix; inflows; outflows; destination categories
safe_use: Safe claim: AUM is a map

first_principles_point: Every money path starts with a source whose return, liquidity, and risk needs shape the route.
money_path: original source -> return/liquidity/risk need -> platform intake -> wrapper selection
company_examples: pensions; insurers; wealth clients; retail funds; sovereigns; bank deposits; institutions
proof_needed: capital source; liability duration; redemption rights; commitment terms; funding cost
safe_use: Safe claim: different sources carry different rights and constraints.

first_principles_point: The wrapper decides liquidity, leverage, reporting, fees, redemption rights, collateral, tax treatment, and payment priority.
money_path: capital source -> legal wrapper -> permitted assets -> leverage and liquidity rules -> cash rights
company_examples: ETFs; BDCs; insurer general accounts; SMAs; private-credit funds; infrastructure funds; CLOs; ABS vehicles
proof_needed: vehicle documents; statutory schedules; BDC filings; fund terms; leverage; redemption terms
safe_use: Safe claim: the wrapper changes the legal meaning of the money.

first_principles_point: Insurance liabilities can become quiet funding sources for long-duration credit and real assets.
money_path: policyholder/annuity buyer -> insurer liability -> invested assets -> credit/infrastructure/structured asset -> investment income -> liability cost -> spread
company_examples: Apollo/Athene; KKR/Global Atlantic; Brookfield Wealth Solutions; Prudential; MetLife; Blackstone insurance SMAs
proof_needed: statutory filings; Schedule D; Schedule BA; investment income; liability cost; asset quality; proceeds
safe_use: Safe claim: insurance AUM needs legal-entity and liability-cost proof.

first_principles_point: Private credit becomes real evidence when a named borrower, facility, lender role, and repayment path are visible.
money_path: institution/insurance/wealth capital -> private-credit vehicle or BDC -> named borrower/facility -> use of proceeds -> interest/repayment -> non-accrual/default/loss check
company_examples: Ares; Apollo; Blackstone; KKR; Carlyle; Blue Owl; BlackRock/HPS; BDCs
proof_needed: borrower list; facility agreement; lender allocation; use of proceeds; cash interest; repayment; non-accruals
safe_use: Safe claim: private credit is a borrower route only when borrower evidence exists.

first_principles_point: Origination is more powerful than passive ownership because it shapes the deal at birth.
money_path: borrower or asset need -> platform origination channel -> negotiated terms -> vehicle allocation -> fee/spread/carry
company_examples: Apollo; Ares; KKR; Blackstone; Brookfield; BlackRock/HPS
proof_needed: origination volume; underwriting terms; covenants; collateral; fees; servicing; allocation
safe_use: Safe claim: origination power needs term and allocation evidence.

first_principles_point: Platform economics are not the same thing as end-investor returns or borrower success.
money_path: AUM or vehicle assets -> management fee/FRE/spread/carry -> platform earnings -> investor net return and borrower outcome still separate
company_examples: Blackstone; KKR; Apollo; Ares; Carlyle; Blue Owl
proof_needed: FRE; management fees; carried interest; distributable earnings; net returns; borrower performance; losses
safe_use: Safe claim: separate platform fee earnings from investor and borrower outcomes.

first_principles_point: A spread is durable only if the route is hard to avoid and the risk cost is lower than the income.
money_path: controlled route -> fee/spread/carry -> losses/funding cost/liquidity cost -> durable or fragile margin
company_examples: banks; insurers; Apollo; KKR; Blackstone; Ares; payment/servicing routes
proof_needed: asset yield; liability cost; management fee yield; loss cost; funding cost; margin; capital
safe_use: Safe claim: spreads need route and risk-cost proof.

first_principles_point: Private platforms are capturing growth in capital routing, but that does not mean banks disappeared or that every private route is safer or better.
money_path: public/institutional/insurance/retail savings -> alternative platform -> private wrapper -> private asset or borrower -> fee/spread/illiquidity/return
company_examples: Blackstone; KKR; Apollo; Ares; Brookfield; BlackRock; Carlyle; Franklin; Invesco
proof_needed: AUM growth; inflows; private-credit deployment; insurance assets; wealth channels; redemption terms
safe_use: Safe claim: private-capital growth is real but not total bank replacement proof.

first_principles_point: Shareholder cash return proves platform monetization, not the final destination's cash quality.
money_path: sticky AUM/permanent capital/insurance assets -> management fees/spread/FRE -> distributable earnings -> dividends/buybacks/reinvestment
company_examples: Blackstone; KKR; Apollo; Ares; BlackRock; Carlyle
proof_needed: dividends; buybacks; distributable earnings; FRE; reinvestment; capital ratios; fee durability
safe_use: Safe claim: capital return is platform proof

first_principles_point: The legal entity is where vague platform language becomes inspectable evidence.
money_path: parent brand -> subsidiary/legal entity -> schedule or vehicle -> instrument -> cash event
company_examples: Athene; Global Atlantic; Brookfield insurers; ARCC; BXSL; FSK; statutory subsidiaries
proof_needed: statutory schedules; BDC schedules; CUSIPs; trustee reports; credit agreements; collateral certificates
safe_use: Safe claim: inspect the legal entity before making named claims.

first_principles_point: Control of data and servicing can matter as much as control of capital.
money_path: asset/borrower -> servicing and monitoring -> performance data -> pricing/allocation/recovery -> platform advantage or conflict
company_examples: Ares; Apollo; Blackstone; Brookfield; BlackRock Aladdin/HPS; servicers
proof_needed: servicing rights; borrower reporting; collateral monitoring; defaults; recoveries; allocation policies
safe_use: Safe claim: data and servicing create advantage and possible conflicts.

first_principles_point: Liquidity terms are part of the return, not a footnote.
money_path: investor capital -> illiquid wrapper -> asset holdings -> redemption request or claim need -> gate/sale/refinancing/liquidity support
company_examples: BREIT-style vehicles; private credit funds; insurers; BDCs; interval funds
proof_needed: redemption terms; gates; liquidity facilities; asset duration; liability duration; valuation marks
safe_use: Safe claim: illiquidity can be rational but must be named.

first_principles_point: Most annual-report platform evidence reaches source, platform, wrapper, and destination levels; full proof needs named asset and cash evidence.
money_path: source -> platform -> wrapper -> destination -> named asset/borrower -> cash proof
proof_needed: source capital; wrapper; asset/borrower; use of proceeds; receipts; income; collateral; waterfall; return model
safe_use: Safe claim: this is the proof standard for capital platforms.

first_principles_point: The next work should create named proof stacks for Apollo/Athene, KKR/Global Atlantic, Blackstone, BlackRock/HPS, Ares, and Brookfield.
money_path: source pull -> legal wrapper -> named asset/borrower -> use/cash evidence -> return bridge
company_examples: Apollo/Athene; KKR/Global Atlantic; Blackstone; BlackRock/HPS; Ares; Brookfield
proof_needed: statutory legal-entity schedules; BDC rows; credit agreements; borrower financials; collateral certificates; debt waterfalls; remittances; return models
safe_use: Safe claim: this page defines the next proof stacks; it is not final named-cash proof.
